title: FP8/INT8 Sprint Daily Notes (working scratchpad)
content:
Context / purpose
- This is the messy daily scratchpad for the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint. Expect shorthand + partial conclusions.
- Goal: reproducible benchmark matrix (microbench + E2E serving) + decisions: kernel auto-select + scheduler knobs + quantization profile defaults + canary thresholds.
- Primary GPUs: H100 + A100. Secondary: L4 “if we have time / if harness supports shapes cleanly”.

Quick links (internal)
- Sprint epic: ENG-7421
- Matrix sheet: fp8-int8-benchmark-matrix-v1 (Drive)
- Metrics defs: fp8-int8-perf-metrics-definitions (Drive)
- Quality summary: quality-vs-quantization-evals-summary (Drive)
- Kickoff thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776401123-fp8-int8-sprint-kickoff.json

Notes glossary (so we’re consistent)
- TTFT = time-to-first-token (p50/p95). Often sensitive to launch overhead, batching window, and prefill scheduling.
- TPOT = time-per-output-token (decode) (p50/p95). Usually reflects steady-state kernel throughput + cache behavior.
- “E2E mixed” = prefill/decode interleaved at typical production ratios; NOT pure prefill or pure decode.
- Always record: git SHA, container tag, CUDA + driver versions, GPU clocks state, MIG/partitioning, region/cluster.


2026-02-10 (Tue) — Kickoff + methodology sign-off
Attendees: Hiro, Sofia, Rina, Grace, Isabella, Jonas, Claire, Neha/Irene (capacity), Allison/Rafael (canary)
- Decisions:
  - We will treat measurement stability as a deliverable (not a “nice to have”). If p95 variance > ~5–7% on stable workloads, we block “wins” from being claimed.
  - Microbench is necessary but insufficient; E2E mixed workloads drive final kernel selection decisions.
  - Default approach for auto-select: conservative, bias to correctness + stable perf. Enable per model + region behind flags.
- Action items:
  - Rina/Isabella: baseline harness sanity run on H100 (single model) w/ clocks locked + warmup rules.
  - Grace/Yuki: list kernel variants we’re comparing (FP8 attention path, INT8 matmul path, baseline).
  - Sofia/Omar/Julian: define 2–3 “mixed workload” profiles (prefill:decode mix, concurrency) to run for E2E.
  - Irene: reserve H100 windows; avoid Dedicated pool impact.
- Link: capacity thread sources/slack/eng-infra/1776409912-h100-capacity-reservation-for-benchmarks.json


2026-02-11 (Wed) — Harness updates progress + first variance report
- Status:
  - PR-19812 (harness toggles + artifact export) in review; needs one more pass on metadata completeness.
  - benchmark-lab PR-842/851 moving; runner can now pin CUDA/driver + optional GPU clocks.
- Blocker:
  - H100 run-to-run variance higher than expected on “baseline decode-only” test (p95 TPOT moving ~10–15%).
  - Initial hypothesis: shared-node contention (other jobs), clocks not truly locked, thermal throttling.
- Decision (quick): no further “full matrix” runs until we can produce stable baselines on 3 repeated runs.
- To investigate:
  - Confirm GPU clock lock is effective (nvidia-smi -lgc). Capture before/after in artifacts.
  - Check if MIG is enabled in the cluster we grabbed.
  - Validate container is exactly pinned (driver mismatch can still occur depending on host).
- Slack: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776408450-benchmark-harness-variance-on-h100.json


2026-02-12 (Thu) — Driver/CUDA mismatch found + workaround
- Finding:
  - Driver version mismatch across clusters (H100 pool A on 550.xx vs pool B on 535.xx). Benchmarks were mixed, causing noise.
  - Confirmed via artifact uploader patch (PR-19880 WIP) and manual checks.
- Mitigation:
  - For the sprint: pin runner to “known-good cluster list” where host driver matches our expected baseline.
  - Longer term: add preflight check to runner: refuse to start if driver/CUDA combo not in allowlist.
- Infra:
  - Irene aligning on two clusters per region that have consistent driver stack.
- Slack: sources/slack/eng-infra/1776428891-driver-version-mismatch-across-clusters.json
- Also:
  - Jonas requested we define “acceptable measurement drift” explicitly for the standards update (Claire to draft wording).


2026-02-13 (Fri) — INT8 correctness failure (shape guard) + harness freeze for weekend runs
- INT8 matmul:
  - Found a correctness failure on an INT8 matmul path for a specific shape regime (likely alignment/stride constraints).
  - Action: add shape guards + fallback to baseline kernels when unsupported.
  - PR-19841 is the home; need unit test w/ offending shape.
- Slack: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776412331-int8-matmul-correctness-failure-shape-guard.json
- Harness:
  - We will freeze harness interface by EOD (flags + measurement loop) so weekend runs don’t chase moving target.
  - Artifact metadata: must include git SHA, model hash, kernel mode, scheduler mode, driver/CUDA, clocks, and workload profile name.
- Weekend plan (if variance stabilized):
  - H100: run top 2 models across 2 workloads (decode-only + mixed).
  - A100: baseline only + one FP8 candidate path if integration is stable.


2026-02-14 (Sat) — Weekend runs start (H100) + early FP8 attention signal
- Isabella ran the first “stable” set on H100 (cluster pinned + clocks locked).
- Early E2E signal:
  - FP8 attention kernel shows clear TPOT improvement in decode-heavy workload (~8–12% p50), but mixed workload TTFT sometimes regresses (small, but p95 moves enough to matter).
- Hypothesis:
  - Launch overhead / kernel selection overhead in prefill path might dominate at low batch / short prompts.
  - Scheduler prefill/decode interleaving might be defeating the kernel win.
- Action:
  - Request Nsight traces for top 3 problematic cases (one TTFT regression, one big win, one neutral).
- Slack: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776425512-request-nsys-traces-for-top-3-cases.json


2026-02-15 (Sun) — More H100 runs + “debug logging” suspicion
- Observed:
  - Some runs show higher CPU overhead (client-side) and higher variance; logs indicate debug-level runtime logging may be enabled in one container.
- Action:
  - Marcus to check for recent debug logging changes impacting perf harness (candidate: PR to gate logging).
  - Put a “logging disabled” check into runner config for benchmark mode.
- Note to self:
  - We need a simple “perf hygiene checklist” before every batch of runs (env vars, logging, clocks, driver).


2026-02-16 (Mon) — Scheduler instrumentation lands + mixed workload definitions stabilized
- Scheduler:
  - PR-19855 adds prefill/decode breakdown, queue depth histograms, backpressure counters.
  - Julian confirms tags will allow slicing by model/GPU/mode once PR-19934 lands (not yet).
- Mixed workload profiles (final-ish names):
  - MIX-A: short prompts, medium generation, concurrency 16 (TTFT-sensitive).
  - MIX-B: medium prompts, longer generation, concurrency 32 (TPOT/throughput-sensitive).
  - PREFILL-only: long prompts (stress prefill kernel).
  - DECODE-only: steady-state decode (stress KV cache + attention).
- Decision:
  - All “claims” in matrix must specify which profile. No mixing/averaging across profiles without footnote.


2026-02-17 (Tue) — FP8 attention TTFT regression thread + proposed guardrail
- Thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776419988-fp8-attention-kernel-regression-ttft.json
- Findings:
  - TTFT regression only appears in MIX-A and mostly on one model family with smaller hidden size.
  - When batching window is reduced, TTFT improves but TPOT drops slightly.
- Proposed guardrail (Hiro + Sofia aligned tentatively):
  - Only select FP8 attention for seq-len regime >= threshold OR when concurrency >= threshold (where throughput wins matter and TTFT regression is less pronounced).
  - Else fall back to baseline attention kernel for TTFT-critical regimes.
- TODO:
  - Yuki to encode guardrail in heuristic PR (PR-19863 / later PR-7430 implementation work).
  - Omar to quantify scheduler parameter sensitivity: does tweaking batching window allow safe FP8 enablement in MIX-A?


2026-02-18 (Wed) — Canary planning starts + noisy alert concerns
- SRE/Obs:
  - Allison draft dashboard dimensions: model/GPU/region/mode, plus TTFT/TPOT/tokens-s, GPU mem, error rate.
  - Rafael: perf canary alerts too noisy with small sample sizes; need noise suppression + minimum sample threshold.
- Thread: sources/slack/eng-sre/1776453320-perf-canary-alerts-too-noisy.json
- Decision:
  - Canary gating must be per model + region (not global). Auto-rollback should only trigger when both (a) threshold breach and (b) sample >= N, OR when absolute error rate spike occurs.
- Open question:
  - What’s our “acceptable” TTFT p95 regression for a canary? (We’ve been using 3%–5% as rough, but need to calibrate vs variance.)


2026-02-19 (Thu) — Heuristics review + metadata completeness
- Heuristics review thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776430817-kernel-autoselect-heuristics-review.json
- Main points:
  - Prefer INT8 matmul in regimes where it’s stable + correctness proven; otherwise FP8 attention is the bigger win for decode-heavy.
  - Must include fallback rules (shape constraints, head dim alignment, KV cache alignment edge cases).
- Metadata:
  - PR-19880: artifact uploader now attaches driver/CUDA, clocks state, model hash, and kernel mode.
  - Remaining gap: scheduler config snapshot and batching window values need to be exported too (Omar/Julian to add).


2026-02-20 (Fri) — First “full-ish” matrix day: H100 top 4 models; A100 baseline + INT8
- H100:
  - Completed baseline + FP8 attention for 4 models across DECODE-only + MIX-B.
  - MIX-A still not fully stable for one model (TTFT p95 variance). Suspect queueing + backpressure interactions.
- A100:
  - Baseline stable.
  - INT8 matmul shows modest gains in prefill-only for one model, neutral elsewhere; correctness guardrails seem to work.
- Blocker:
  - “KV cache alignment” edge case suspected when FP8 decode hits certain seq-len boundaries (saw step-function in TPOT).
  - Grace flagged a candidate fix PR (PR-19871).


2026-02-21 (Sat) — KV cache alignment fix tested + scheduling knob tradeoffs
- PR-19871 (KV cache alignment) appears to eliminate the step-function TPOT spikes in our problematic case.
- Scheduler knob discussion (thread): sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776439004-scheduler-knobs-batching-window-tradeoffs.json
- Takeaways:
  - To realize FP8 wins E2E, we may need to tune batching window + backpressure defaults slightly (especially in MIX-B).
  - But tightening the window improves TTFT; loosening improves throughput; we need per-tier/per-mode defaults? (or at least a “benchmark mode” vs “prod mode” alignment.)
- Action:
  - Sofia/Lena to propose “new default” for mixed workloads that improves realized kernel gains without hurting TTFT.


2026-02-22 (Sun) — Debug logging regression confirmed + fix in flight
- Marcus confirmed a debug logging path impacted benchmark timings for a subset of runs.
- PR-19918 created to gate/remove debug logging in benchmark mode.
- Note:
  - Need to annotate matrix sheet to mark which runs are “invalidated” due to logging.


2026-02-23 (Mon) — Canary gate implementation + first region cohort discussion
- PR-19896 adds per model/region gating + rollback logic.
- Rollout planning thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776451055-canary-plan-which-regions-first.json
- Proposed canary order (tentative):
  - Start in one low-traffic region with good observability + stable fleet config, then expand.
  - Avoid eu-west first due to prior customer sensitivity + mixed driver footprint (needs confirmation).
- Open items:
  - Ensure metrics tagging includes model/GPU/kernel-mode (PR-19934) before canary is meaningful.


2026-02-24 (Tue) — Matrix status + remaining gaps
- Status thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776442209-benchmark-matrix-status-and-gaps.json
- Gaps:
  - A100: missing MIX-A for 2 models (runner queued behind other jobs; needs reserved window).
  - H100: missing prefill-only long prompt profile for 1 model (job failed; needs rerun).
  - L4: not started. Might be out of scope unless we get a clean day.
- Decision:
  - We ship decisions based on H100/A100; L4 is “best effort” and will be documented as such.


2026-02-25 (Wed) — Canary detected TTFT regression -> auto rollback (good) + triage
- Event:
  - Perf canary flagged TTFT p95 spike in one region/model combination after enabling FP8 attention.
  - Auto rollback triggered as designed.
- Thread: sources/slack/eng-sre/1776464884-canary-detected-ttft-regression-auto-rollback.json
- Triage notes:
  - It was a TTFT regression only; TPOT was better. Error rates normal.
  - Sample size was borderline; still crossed the configured “min sample” threshold.
  - Need to validate whether scheduler knob config differed in that region (config drift?)
- Action items:
  - Rafael: confirm region’s runtime config matches expected scheduler defaults.
  - Yuki: add heuristic guardrail for that shape regime (likely small hidden size + low concurrency).
  - Allison: update dashboard to highlight “config version” / “heuristic version” as a tag (if possible).


2026-02-26 (Thu) — Hotfix disable FP8 for specific shape regime + quality check reminder
- Hotfix:
  - PR-19941 disables FP8 kernel for a specific shape regime discovered during canary (fallback to baseline).
- Applied ML:
  - Jonas/Arjun reminder: even if perf is good, enabling by default requires eval sign-off for each model family.
  - Long-context FP8 quality regression remains a concern for one model (see eng-ml thread; not reproduced by runtime team yet).
- To investigate:
  - Make sure matrix includes at least one long-context profile for the model family where quality issues were flagged (even if just to bound the perf behavior).


2026-02-27 (Fri) — Release flag defaults discussion + “what we can claim” list
- Thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/1776460021-release-1-22-0-flag-defaults.json
- Notes:
  - Default state should be “off” globally at release, “on” only for approved model/GPU pairs in approved regions.
  - Need a simple table in release notes: (model family x GPU) -> default mode (baseline/FP8/INT8) + caveats.
- Product/perf transparency:
  - Henry pinged: we need footnotes for benchmark claims (driver/CUDA pinned, clocks locked, workload profile definitions, sample sizes).
  - Claire to draft the “minimum disclosure” list for anything shared externally.


2026-02-28 (Sat) — Wrap-up notes / remaining TODOs
- What feels done:
  - Harness is usable + artifacts are much more reproducible (driver/CUDA/clocks/mode captured).
  - We have a defensible H100/A100 matrix for top models across DECODE-only + MIX-B; MIX-A coverage is partial but enough to identify TTFT-sensitive regressions.
  - Canary rollback worked in real conditions; hotfix path is clear.
- What is not done / follow-ups:
  - L4 coverage (likely punt; document explicitly).
  - Formalize “variance budget” and minimum repetitions per profile (Claire + Rina).
  - Finish metrics tagging (PR-19934) + ensure dashboards slice cleanly.
  - Close the loop on quality sign-offs (Jonas/Arjun) for any default enablement.
  - Write the “regression triage playbook” delta (what to check first: clocks/driver/config drift/logging).

Open questions (carry into next week)
1) Do we want separate heuristic thresholds for Hosted vs Dedicated? Dedicated customers are often TTFT-sensitive and hate jitter.
2) Should scheduler knobs be coupled to kernel mode (FP8 vs baseline) or remain global defaults?
3) What is the “safe” perf canary threshold profile per GPU SKU (H100 vs A100)? One size doesn’t fit.

Random notes / reminders
- Always invalidate runs when: driver mismatch, clocks not locked, debug logging on, obvious cluster contention.
- When TTFT regresses but TPOT improves: check batching window + prefill queue depth first, then kernel launch overhead.
- When TPOT spikes step-wise: suspect KV cache alignment, seq-len boundary effects, or shape falling back to less optimal kernel.
